Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Private VPC: edge fabric segmentation + access-gateway ops review

Hi Lena / Orbit team,

Thanks again for making time. Attached is v2 of the edge fabric proposal and the segmentation mock (moc-segmentation-diagram.drawio). The two things we'd like to validate with your ops/security folks this week: 

- Control plane/data plane demarcation at the tenant access gateway (we propose an L3 hop with explicit ACLs so the control plane (management, K8s API access) never traverses tenant-data paths).
- Egress channels and NAT expectations for short-lived inference jobs (we're proposing a per-tenant egress proxy lane with transparent source-NAT and a shared egress pool).

Quick asks before Monday's review call: 
1) Can you confirm whether Orbit can terminate mTLS at the access-gateway in front of our dedicated nodes (we prefer mutual TLS termination at the gateway for customer certs)?
2) Any hard requirements on port ranges or ACLs for your onprem connectors?
3) If we route control-plane traffic to your management VLAN, do you need a separate VRF or is tagging + ACL sufficient?

I've flagged a proposed cutover / canary plan in the proposal (section 4) — would like to align on rollback criteria.

Attachments: vpc-edge-fabric-proposal_v2.pdf, moc-segmentation-diagram.drawio, egress-policy-srd.md

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Weber <lena@orbitcloud.com>

Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 14:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private VPC: edge fabric segmentation + access-gateway ops review

Hi Priya / team,

Thanks — had a quick pass with our network engineering leads. High-level notes: 

- mTLS termination at Orbit access-gateway: yes, we can terminate mutual TLS for customer certs. We prefer certs to be presented at the TLS layer and will hand back validated client info via an X-Client-ID header to your upstream (we'll provide the header contract).
- Port/ACLs: we'll need 1024-65535 for ephemeral outbound ephemeral ports for inference bursts plus static TCP 443/80 for control plane. We can narrow ephemeral ranges if you require.
- VRF vs tagging: tagging + ACL + SVI per tenant is our standard approach. For stronger tenant guarantees we can place the control plane on a single management VRF; that approach adds ~6-8ms additional hop in our lab but isolates routing tables.

We reviewed your canary rollback criteria — suggested addition: include token-loss threshold >1% and KV-cache miss-rate delta >20% as additional abort signals.

I've attached a sample ACL template (we'll upload a combined config stubbing to the Drive folder before Monday).

Cheers,
Lena
Site Reliability Lead, Orbit Cloud
Lena@orbitcloud.com
